primitives.name: Speed Curve Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: iSH lane = data prep, kinematic feature code (stdlib), viz prototypes (matplotlib), the EPA scoring harness.
primitives.assumptions: Trajectory data is sampled at 10 Hz; motion is continuous and differentiable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At t = 0, v(0) = 0; at peak speed, a(t) = 0.

layer2.mapping: Maps velocity profiles to performance indicators such as top speed and acceleration time, used in EPA scoring.
layer2.telemetry: EPA per game, normalized by position group

primitives.name: Change of Direction Kinematics
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Pose estimation on public combine video** (MediaPipe BlazePose 33-keypoint on drill clips from NFL.com/YouTube): joint angles, arm-drive amplitude, trunk lean, ground-contact timing, stance type (3-pt vs 2-pt) — things 10Hz hip-tag tracking cannot see.
primitives.assumptions: Heading angle derivative is measurable; body orientation is tracked via pose estimation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When v(t) approaches zero, \kappa(t) becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Pose-derived joint angles and stance type inform COD arc radius and speed retention, aligning with NGS-derived COD metrics.
layer2.telemetry: COD arc radius, speed retention ratio

primitives.name: Rhythm and Planarity Metrics
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Game-film CV** = STRETCH, not core (no public play-synced video; mark as future work in the writeup).
primitives.assumptions: Lateral motion is periodic; path efficiency is computed from actual vs. straight-line distance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In static or non-moving states, f_lateral ≈ 0.

layer2.mapping: Lateral oscillation frequency and path efficiency are used to detect false-step patterns and movement economy in game scenarios.
layer2.telemetry: False-step detection rate, average path efficiency

Speed curves capture dynamic acceleration and deceleration, while COD metrics reflect agility and control under load. Rhythm and planarity provide insight into movement economy and consistency. Dualities emerge in how 10Hz tracking and CV-based metrics complement each other—kinematics alone may miss biomechanical nuances, while CV lacks temporal fidelity.
